name: agung
title: Agung
builder: drum: tones 110 Hz, ring 0.45 s (the large, low pangandungan, from the source; damped by hand, from the source), 290 Hz level 0.35, ring 0.3 s and 655 Hz level 0.25, ring 0.3 s (the bossed gong's inharmonic upper partials); noise 0.15, low pass 600 Hz, ring 0.03 s (the rubber-padded mallet, from the source); tail 0.45 s
notes: Unpitched (a fixed tone). Agung page: 'is a set of two wide-rimmed, vertically suspended gongs used by the Maguindanao, Maranao, Sama-Bajau and Tausug people of the Philippines'; 'The agung is a large, heavy, wide-rimmed gong shaped like a kettle gong'; 'The larger, lower pitched gong of the two is called the pangandungan by the Maguindanao'; 'The mallets, called balu, are made from short sticks about half a foot in length and padded with soft but tough material such as rubber at one end'; 'A series of solid, fast decaying sounds are produced using dampening techniques. The desired effect is produced after striking the knob, by leaving one's hand or knee or the mallets themselves on it'. Built as the larger gong of the pair (the pangandungan), struck on its knob with a padded mallet and damped: a deep bossed-gong tone that dies quickly, with only a soft, dark mallet thump. From the source: a large, heavy bossed gong (a low tone with a clear pitch), the rubber-padded mallet (dark, quiet noise, no click), the damping (a short ring). The page names the pitches of the pair (lower, higher) but gives no note or compass, so the tone is fixed and ignores the pitch given, as for tabla bayan. Told apart (rule 7) from the catalog tam tam (a flat gong's crash: 72 and 133 Hz ringing 6 s under loud noise) and wind gong (noise ringing 3 s) by its damped, pitched tone; from the tuned gong in tuned percussion (rings 5 s, follows the pitch) by the damping; from the toms, bombo leguero and kendang ageng (membranes: a falling glide, two parts; kendang ageng 80 and 250 Hz under a hand slap) by a steady metal tone with two inharmonic partials and no slap. Every tone, glide, ring, noise band, level, drive and tail in the builder is sound design (no fetched source gives a number).

name: bell tree

notes: Bell tree page: 'consisting of vertically nested inverted metal bowls'; 'The number of bowls can vary between approximately 14 and 28'; 'An effective glissando is produced by sliding a triangle beater, a glockenspiel mallet, or a xylophone mallet down the length of the tree'; 'The bell tree is often used to accentuate the start or end of passages of music with a "bright", "shimmer" effect'. name: bossed gong

notes: Another name for the catalog tuned gong (tuned percussion).
